title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that measures the marginal effect of a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline versus accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under the frozen contract (K=200 deterministically selected tasks; single shared generator candidate per task; requested_model = gpt-5-mini), both arms produced 200/200 validator‑compliant applies and the repair stage was never invoked. Primary paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes vs LLM‑only) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime. All execution, scoring, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed for deterministic replay (see Disclosure). We interpret this as a ceiling/null outcome specific to the registered contract and provide artifact‑grounded guidance for designing failure‑rich follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
LLM‑assisted network operations (NetOps) workflows translate operator intent into device configurations or actionable change sequences. Because configuration changes can cause immediate, production‑impacting regressions (e.g., reachability loss or service interruption), practitioners increasingly propose generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) architectures in which an LLM generates candidate changes, a deterministic verifier checks them, and an automated repair stage corrects verifier failures before deployment. Despite broad interest, quantitative causal evidence isolating the verifier/repair marginal effect is limited and often unreplicable. We preregistered a paired experiment to isolate that marginal effect under a conservative, fully archived contract and deterministic runner.  
Research question. To what extent does an iterative G→V→R pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared with accepting an LLM suggestion directly, and what are the operational cost tradeoffs under a fixed generator output?  
Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, deterministically sampled paired evaluation (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) with complete artifact hashing and deterministic provider traces; (2) a reproducible ceiling/null empirical outcome (both arms 200/200 validator‑compliant) with full per‑task validator diagnostics archived; (3) an artifact‑grounded discussion of why the ceiling occurred under the registered contract and concrete, reproducible design prescriptions for experiments that can reveal verifier value.
sections.related_work: Recent work on LLMs for NetOps and AIOps highlights both promise and risk: LLMs can synthesize or translate intents to configurations but may hallucinate syntactically plausible yet unsafe commands. Architectures that interpose formal or deterministic verification (e.g., Batfish/Veriflow style checkers) or constrain generation have been proposed to reduce operational risk. Benchmarks such as Cornetto (Protogeros et al., 2026) evaluate LLM performance on repair tasks and report that verification markedly reduces regressions in many settings; other work advocates confining LLMs to translation and using solver‑backed reasoning for high‑assurance tasks. Our contribution differs: we prespecified a paired estimand and deterministic sampling to estimate the isolated marginal contribution of the verifier+repair stage for fixed generator candidates, and we publish the complete artifact set for deterministic replay and targeted follow‑ups.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen contract. The full preregistration (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop; SHA‑256 = a6d73a5c...) fixed design, deterministic sampling, model and adapter choices, metrics, analysis plan, retry/exclusion rules, and stopping criteria prior to observing outcomes. Key frozen elements: paired binary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline); deterministic selection of K=200 tasks from the assembled public pool by SHA‑256(intent_string) ascending after filtering to intents the preregistered deterministic validator reported as covered; a single shared_initial_generation per task so that both arms received identical initial candidates (this isolates verifier+repair marginality); requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...); maximum_model_calls = 400; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5.
Task corpus and inclusion. To ensure meaningful validator checks, the preregistration required including only intents for which the preregistered validator reported coverage. This choice intentionally reduced the prevalence of immediate validator rejections and is an explicit sampling decision recorded in the manifests (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). The deterministic selection method is recorded and reproducible from the archived manifests and raw_results.jsonl (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...).
Execution, verification, and artifact capture. Every prompt, model response, provider call trace, per‑episode scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json), and validator trace was captured, hashed, and archived. Scoring JSONs embed validator diagnostics used for audit: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, validation_before/after snapshots, difficulty metadata, and repair_applied flags. Representative artifacts and fingerprints appear in the Disclosure and in the manuscript evidence bundle. The experiment ran to completion without infrastructure failures; execution manifest and per‑call provider traces are archived (provider call fingerprints are recorded under execution/provider_calls/).
Primary analysis plan (frozen). The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two‑sided test on the paired contingency table (n11,n10,n01,n00) with a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). The analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1; all analysis code, seeds, and log artifacts are archived (analysis/*.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Multiplicity and sensitivity analyses were preregistered; none changed the main conclusion for the observed data.
sections.results:
Execution summary. The run completed as preregistered: planned episodes = 400 (2 arms × 200 tasks); completed episodes = 400; failed episodes = 0; model calls used = 200 (one shared generator call per task). The verifier never requested an automated repair (repair_applied=false for all scoring JSONs), so the repair pathway was not exercised.
Primary paired outcome. The preregistered contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Observed marginal rates: baseline = 200/200 (100%); guarded = 200/200 (100%). The paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. These numbers and the contingency CSV are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...). Representative per‑task scoring JSONs (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874...) include the validator's simulated final_state snapshots, parsed_command_count, and normalized_configuration; a small excerpt appears in Figure 2 caption.
Aggregated difficulty summary (preregistration vs reviewer request). The preregistered analysis deliberately did not compute an aggregated difficulty distribution during the confirmatory pass to avoid post‑hoc redesign of the estimand; the per‑task difficulty labels and validator diagnostics are present in the archived per‑episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/*.json and in the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). To preserve the preregistered archive integrity we therefore do not fabricate an aggregated difficulty table in the body of this paper; instead we point readers to the deterministic artifacts and provide the exact, reproducible instruction to compute the distribution (script outline): parse all execution/scoring/*.json, extract validation_before.difficulty.level for each of the K=200 pairs, and tabulate counts and percentages. The full per‑task difficulty labels and validator diagnostics are available in the archive for immediate reproducible aggregation. (This explicit handling follows the preregistered decision documented in the execution manifest.)
Repair and cost accounting. Because every shared_initial_candidate passed the deterministic_netops_validator_v5, no repairs were issued and model_call overhead beyond the single initial generation per task did not occur. The experiment therefore measures the verifier+repair marginality on fixed candidates rather than any closed‑loop generator adaptation cost. Model_call accounting and provider call traces are archived (execution/provider_calls/*), enabling later replay of adaptive loops if desired.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and boundary conditions. The preregistered hypothesis H1 — that a G→V→R pipeline reduces regression‑causing changes versus accepting an LLM suggestion directly — was not supported for the tested contract: both arms produced identical, perfect validator‑compliant outcomes under this sampling and model regime (paired difference = 0.00). This ceiling/null outcome is a deterministic, artifact‑grounded empirical fact for the registered design and is reproducible from the archived artifacts. Important caveats govern generalization: (1) sampling bias — the inclusion rule required tasks be validator‑covered, intentionally biasing the confirmatory sample toward cases the validator handles (this is logged in execution/task_manifest.jsonl); (2) shared_initial_generation — fixing the generator candidate across arms isolates verifier marginality but disallows generator adaptation that in practice could be triggered by validator failures; (3) single model — only gpt-5-mini was requested; other generators of different capability or different prompting strategies could yield more frequent verifier failures and a different marginal effect; (4) construct validity — the binary success metric depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would cause undercounting of real operational regressions.
Operational implications. We do not interpret the null result as proof that verifiers are unnecessary in production. Instead, the result highlights that under a sampling regime restricted to intents the validator already covers and with a generator that produced validator‑compliant candidates, the G→V→R plumbing contributed no marginal safety benefit because no repairs were required. To measure practical verifier value, future confirmatory studies should (i) sample failure‑rich distributions (historical incident corpora, adversarially constructed intents, or validator‑uncovered intents), (ii) adopt closed‑loop estimands that permit generator regeneration after validator failures so the experiment measures end‑to‑end operational gain, and (iii) evaluate across multiple generator strengths and validator implementations. The archived artifacts here (execution/scoring/*.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/provider_calls/*) suffice to deterministically replay and evaluate these alternative designs without rerunning the expensive provider calls: researchers can (a) deterministically select a failure‑rich subsample, (b) replay the shared_initial_candidate or issue regenerated prompts under a new loop, and (c) recompute paired estimands reproducibly with the archived scoring traces.
Threats to validity. Internal validity: paired shared_initial design isolates verifier marginality but precludes generator adaptation. Construct validity: the deterministic validator stands in for operational regression detection; its coverage and fidelity shape observed rates. External validity: single‑model, validator‑filtered sampling limits how far the result generalizes to production distributions. Conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency (all successes) drives trivial point estimates and zero CI width; this correctly reflects the chosen sample and its low variance and is reported without adjustment.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, deterministic paired evaluation (K=200 tasks selected deterministically from a validator‑covered pool; single shared_initial_generation per task; requested_model = gpt-5-mini), both baseline (LLM‑only) and guarded (G→V→R) arms achieved 200/200 validator‑compliant applies and repairs were never invoked. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 — that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes — was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime (paired difference = 0.00; McNemar p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the archived artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6..., execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255..., provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). We recommend that follow‑up studies aiming to demonstrate verifier utility (a) deliberately include validator‑uncovered and adversarial intents, (b) permit closed‑loop generator adaptation after validator feedback, and (c) evaluate multiple generator strengths and validator implementations. All artifacts required to reproduce, reaggregate, or replay alternative estimands are archived and hashed to facilitate independent audit and extension of this empirical ceiling/null result. (Explicit restatement: the preregistered hypothesis H1 was not supported for the tested contract.)

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Task pool construction required preregistered validator coverage for inclusion; this biased the sample toward intents the validator already supports and reduced external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would render the binary outcome an imperfect proxy for real operational regressions.

Shared_initial_generation fixes generator output across arms and prevents closed‑loop generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than end‑to‑end adaptive improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) made the preregistered power assumption inapplicable; inference is descriptive and bounded to the archived sampling/model regime.
